newsitem.title: CANADA: Cricket-India cruise to victory over Pakistan in Canada.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-India cruise to victory over Pakistan in Canada.

text.p: A magnificent, unbeaten 89 from captain Sachin Tendulkar helped India coast to an eight wicket victory over Pakistan on Monday in the first of five limited over cricket matches for the Sahara Cup in Toronto.

Tendulkar faced just 89 balls and struck nine fours and three sixes in an innings of controlled aggression, which capped a fine captain's outing and earned the 23-year-old the player of the match award.
Both teams were restricted to a maximum of 33 overs after umpires delayed the start for four and half hours to allow the ground to dry, following three days of heavy rain.
After being sent in, Pakistan got off to a flying start but lost six wickets for the addition of just 44 runs at one stage and could manage only 170-9 off their 33 overs.

India lost the wicket of makeshift opener Nayan Mongia (9) when the score was just 18, but two half century partnerships lifted Tendulkar's side to 173-2 off just 29.5 overs for an impressive victory.
Tendulkar took the game by the scuff of the neck soon after he was joined by Rahul Dravid (39), the pair adding 90.
However, the young Indian skipper was probably lucky to be there at the end, having survived a series of loud and warranted lbw appeals from Waqar Younis in just the third over of the match.
His dismissal could have turned the match around in front of the tiny crowd of 750, in a stadium with makeshift stands for 5,000.
But Pakistan captain Wasim Akram chose to concentrate on his team's mediocre performance rather than to dwell on their misfortune.
"It is a wake-up call for us," said the all-rounder, who led the team to a Test series victory over England this summer.
"We will have to field, bat and bowl much better tomorrow."
Akram said Pakistan hoped to include Mushtaq Ahmed in the side for the second match of the rain-plagued series. The leg spinner missed Monday's opener because of illness.
"We will be a different side," Akram said. "Mentally they were tougher than us today."
Tendulkar said he was "happy" to get a win after a disappointing series in Sri Lanka where he tentaatively took over the reins as captain.

India set up their victory with some fine bowling from rapid fire leg spinner Avil Kumble (three for 32) and paceman Javagal Srinath (three for 23) and an uncustomary display of tight fielding, which restricted Pakistan after opener Saeed Anwar (46) had got them off to a flying start.
"We have been working at our fielding and today it really paid off," Tendulkar said after striking his 27th half century in one-day internationals.
Organisers were disappointed with the spectator turnout, but pleased simply to get the series underway after rain forced the postponement of matches on Saturday and Sunday.

Four more matches (on Tuesday, Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday) will be played at the small but beautifully groomed Toronto Cricket, Skating and Curling club, mainly for the benefit of tens of millions of fans in Asia watching the rare series on television.
Teams:
Pakistan - Aamir Sohail, Saeed Anwar, Ijaz Ahmed, Inzamam-ul-Haq, Shahdab Kabir, Saleem Malik, Wasim Akram (c) Moin Khan, Saqlain Mushtaq, Azhar Mahmood, Waqar Younis
India - Sachin Tendulkar (c), Ajay Jadeja, Mohammad Azharuddin, Sourav Ganguly, Rahul Dravid, Vinod Kambli, Sunil Joshi, Nayan Mongia, Anil Kumble, Javagal Srinath, B.K. Venkatesh Prasad
